title: Polynomials and Rational Functions
subtitle: Read structure from factors, evaluate polynomial remainders, transform graphs, and manage rational-function domains.

isi.content: A polynomial is an expression made from constants and variables with nonnegative integer exponents. For example, \(3x^4-2x^2+7x-1\) is a polynomial.

items.title: Degree
items.content: The greatest exponent with a nonzero coefficient. The degree of \(3x^4-2x^2+7x-1\) is 4.

items.title: Coefficient
items.content: A number multiplying a variable, such as 3 in \(3x^4\).

items.title: Constant term
items.content: A term with no variable, such as \(-1\).

isi.content: Arrange polynomial terms in descending degree when simplifying or comparing expressions.
Add or subtract like terms, and multiply by distributing every term. Like terms have the same variable part and exponent.

isi.title: Example: addition
isi.content: Add \((2x^2+3x+1)+(x^2-2x+4)\) by combining like terms: \(3x^2+x+5\).

isi.title: Example: multiplication
isi.content: Distribute each term in \((x+3)(x-2)\): \(x^2-2x+3x-6=x^2+x-6\).

items: Keep unlike powers separate: \(x^2\) and \(x\) are not like terms.
Use the distributive property for every term in a product.
Check the degree of the product against the degrees of its factors.

isi.content: If \(x-r\) is a factor of a polynomial, then \(x=r\) is a zero and the graph has an x-intercept at \((r,0)\).

items.title: Odd multiplicity
items.content: The graph usually crosses the x-axis at the zero.

items.title: Even multiplicity
items.content: The graph usually touches the x-axis and turns around.

items.title: Distinct zeros
items.content: The degree can exceed the number of distinct x-intercepts when roots repeat or are nonreal.

isi.content: Read the zero using the opposite sign: the factor \(x+5\) gives the zero \(x=-5\).

isi.title: Example: vertical shift
isi.content: If \(f(x)=7x^3\) and the graph shifts down 2 units, then \(g(x)=7x^3-2\).

isi.title: Example: horizontal shift
isi.content: If \(g(x)=f(x+4)\), the graph of \(f\) moves 4 units to the left. The sign inside the parentheses works opposite to the direction of the shift.
\[\text{The remainder when }P(x)\text{ is divided by }x-c\text{ is }P(c).\]
This theorem often avoids polynomial long division. Substitute the value of \(c\) directly into the polynomial.

isi.title: Example: evaluate a remainder
isi.content: For \(P(x)=x^3-2x+5\), the remainder when dividing by \(x-2\) is \(P(2)=2^3-2(2)+5=9\).
If the divisor is \(x+3\), rewrite it as \(x-(-3)\). The remainder is then \(P(-3)\).
A rational function has the form \(f(x)=\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)}\). Its domain excludes every value that makes the original denominator equal to zero.

isi.title: Example: canceling a common factor
isi.content: For \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-5x+6}{x-2}\), factor the numerator: \(f(x)=\dfrac{(x-2)(x-3)}{x-2}=x-3\), but only for \(x\ne2\). The original excluded value remains excluded.

items: Set the original denominator equal to zero to find restrictions.
State canceled values as excluded from the domain.
Check that an input is in the domain before evaluating.

isi.content: The graph of a polynomial can reveal zeros, multiplicities, and overall behavior. The leading term controls the end behavior, while the factors identify x-intercepts.

items.title: Degree
items.content: A degree-\(n\) polynomial has at most \(n\) real zeros and exactly \(n\) complex zeros when multiplicity is counted.

items.title: Leading coefficient
items.content: The sign of the leading coefficient helps determine whether the ends rise or fall.

items.title: x-intercepts
items.content: Distinct real roots correspond to distinct points where the graph meets the x-axis.

isi.content: Use a graph as a check, but read the scale and the labels carefully. A visible crossing and a tangency represent different root multiplicities.

materi.judul: A reliable polynomial and rational-function workflow

items: Inspect factors and denominators before expanding.
Use zeros to interpret factors and graph intercepts.
Use substitution for direct function values and Remainder Theorem questions.
Apply transformations with careful attention to inside-versus-outside signs.
Write domain restrictions before canceling rational factors.
Use Desmos to verify roots, shifts, holes, and graph behavior.

isi.content: When a source question has a missing graph or incomplete definition, rebuild the mathematical relationship from the stated topic before solving.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=(x+6)(x+5)(x-4)\), which table represents \(y=f(x)-3\)?
discussion: At \(x=-6,-5,4\), one factor of \(f(x)\) is zero, so \(f(x)=0\).
The correct table is choice B.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=x^3+9\), what is \(f(2)\)?
discussion: The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: Given \(k(x)=x^3+110\), what is \(k(2)\)?
discussion: The correct answer is choice A.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=7x^3\), the graph of \(g(x)\) is the graph of \(f(x)\) shifted down 2 units. Which defines \(g\)?
discussion: A vertical shift down 2 subtracts 2 from every output.

latihan.question: A polynomial graph has exactly three distinct x-intercepts. For how many distinct values of \(x\) does the polynomial equal zero?
discussion: An x-intercept occurs where the polynomial value is zero.
Three distinct x-intercepts therefore correspond to three distinct values of \(x\).
The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=x^5+9x+17\), the graph passes through \((0,b)\). What is \(b\)?
Given \(g(x)=x(x-2)(x+6)^2\), the value of \(g(7-w)\) is 0. What is the sum of all possible values of \(w\)?
discussion: Set \(7-w\) equal to each zero: \(w=7\), \(w=5\), or \(w=13\).

latihan.question: Given \(y=2(x-d)(x+d)(x+g)(x-d)\), where \(d\) and \(g\) are distinct positive constants, how many distinct x-intercepts does the graph have?
discussion: The root \(x=d\) is repeated, but it still represents only one distinct x-intercept.
Because \(d\) and \(g\) are distinct and positive, the three roots are distinct, so choice B is correct.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=(x-1)(x+3)(x-2)\), the graph is shifted up 6 units to create \(g\). If \(g(4)=b\), what is \(b\)?
A polynomial has roots \(-1\), \(-3\), and \(5\). Which is a factor?
discussion: A root \(r\) corresponds to the factor \(x-r\).
The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: A polynomial graph crosses the x-axis at exactly two positive points \((a,0)\) and \((b,0)\). Which could define \(f\)?
discussion: The factors \(x-a\) and \(x-b\) create the positive roots \(a\) and \(b\).
Choice A has exactly those two roots and no required additional root.
The correct answer is choice A.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-6x+3}{x-1}\), what is \(f(-1)\)?
discussion: The correct answer is choice A.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=\dfrac{1}{6x}\), what is \(f(3)\)?
discussion: The correct answer is choice D.

latihan.question: If \(f(x)=\dfrac{6}{x}\) and \(g(x)=f(x+4)\), which equation defines \(g\)?
discussion: This is also a shift of the graph 4 units to the left.
The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: The table gives \(g(x)\), where \(g(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{x+3}\) and \(f\) is linear. What is the y-intercept of \(y=f(x)\)?
discussion: The line through \((-9,0)\) and \((21,120)\) has slope \(4\).
Using \((-9,0)\), the equation is \(f(x)=4x+36\), so the y-intercept is \((0,36)\), choice A.

latihan.question: Given \(h(x)=\dfrac{x^2+3x-28}{x+7}\), if \(h(a)=13\) and \(a\) is in the domain of \(h\), what is \(a\)?
discussion: Set \(a-4=13\): \(a=17\), which is in the domain. Choice D is correct.

additionalPractice.question: Factor \(x^2-8x+15\).
discussion: The numbers \(-3\) and \(-5\) multiply to 15 and add to \(-8\).

additionalPractice.question: Find the remainder when \(P(x)=x^3-2x+5\) is divided by \(x-2\).
discussion: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(2)\).

additionalPractice.question: Find the zeros of \(f(x)=(x-2)(x+5)(x-7)\).
discussion: Set each factor equal to zero: \(x-2=0\), \(x+5=0\), and \(x-7=0\).

additionalPractice.question: A polynomial has roots \(-2\), 3, and 5. Write one possible factored form.
discussion: One possible polynomial is \((x+2)(x-3)(x-5)\). Any nonzero constant multiple has the same roots.

additionalPractice.question: The function \(\dfrac{x^2-5x+6}{x-2}\) is defined for \(x\ne2\). Write an equivalent expression on its domain.
discussion: Cancel the common factor only on the original domain: \(f(x)=x-3\) for \(x\ne2\).
The excluded value \(x=2\) must remain excluded.

additionalPractice.question: A rational function has denominator \((x-4)(x+1)\). State its domain restrictions.
discussion: Set each denominator factor equal to zero: \(x-4=0\) and \(x+1=0\).
The denominator is zero at 4 and \(-1\), so both values are excluded from the domain.
